1 طَحَلَهُ , (S, O, K,) aor.
طَحَلَ , inf. n. طَحْلٌ and طَحَلٌ, (K,) He hit, or hurt, his طِحَال [or spleen]. (S, O, K.) ＝
-A2- And طَحَلَهُ, (O, K,) aor.
طَحَلَ , (K,) inf. n. طَحْلٌ, (O,) He filled it; (O, K;) namely, a vessel. (O.) ＝
-A3- طَحِلَ, (S, O, Msb, K,) aor.
طَحَلَ , (Msb, K,) inf. n. طَحَلٌ, (S, O, Msb,) He had a complaint of his طِحَال [or spleen]: (S:) or he became large in his طِحَال: (O, Msb, K:) and طُحِلَ, like عُنِىَ, inf. n. طَحْلٌ, [accord. to the CK طَحَلٌ,] has the former of these two meanings. (K, TA.) ―
-b2- And طَحِلَ, (K, TA,) inf. n. طَحَلٌ, (TA,) He was, or became, of the colour termed طُحْلَة; said of a wolf; and in like manner one says of a sheep or goat. (K, TA.) ―
-b3- And طَحِلَ said of water, (S, O, K,) as also طَهِلَ, (S, O,) It was, or became, corrupt, (S, O, K,) and altered in odour, (S, O,) or stinking, by reason of black mud. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
